I'm moving in on Sept. 11, and classes start on Sept. 14. If it helps, my books are already reserved, and I'm majoring in Microbiology. I'm enrolled in 15 credit hours, plus I have 3 credits from the AP Psych exam.
What are some tips for someone heading off to college?
Put a little bit of time aside for yourself. You'll lose your mind if you don't.
Little bit suspect on how every other comment was down voated but yours...
when you get to your 3-year this will definitely help.
It's a great breeding ground for potentially harmful biofilm and fungal matter. For the eww factor small room + roommates lead to a pretty predictable use for showers as well.

Schedule your classes early in the day (coffee!). Eat afterwards, then study In the library. Go home. Nap. Get up, eat again, play-seriously, have fun! But not too much fun, cuz, you know, early classes.
Oh god. This would have killed me. I am not a morning person at all...
I'm more of a middle of the day person. Class. Eat lunch. Class. Go home. Study. Jerk off to seal information in your head.
Don't blindly follow your adviser. Read the catalog.
Study... drink until you feel good than stop. Don't be that wasted person no one likes that person.

If you're going to sleep in class just don't go. You won't be doing any good and it's distracting to everyone else. If you're going to eat in class make sure it doesn't smell or make noise. No one is making you go to class and if you don't want to go you don't have to. This is a double edged sword as it allows you to work on other things or skip if you know the class won't be worth going into for the day (various reasons for this) but you can get lazy and just stop going which is bad. don't just not go to class to screw around. Have a reason for skipping if you need to. I generally allowed myself to skip once per class per quarter.

Generally speaking if you are pulling all nighters you fucked up somewhere down the line. Take good notes, pay attention and have dedicated study times and/or places (such as the library) and you'll be fine.

If you find yourself writing papers look for an on-campus writing center. Generally there will be a place where students can get their papers proof read. At my school they would then email the teacher that the paper is for to inform them that you went there. This shows the teacher you're really trying and they might be nicer to you if you're struggling.

Go and meet your teachers, advisers, TAs. They won't all become your friends but it's good to be known in your department and teachers can be more lenient if they know you.

There is a good chance you'll have a class that you suck at. Ask the teacher/ Ta for help and they might let it slide. I took a year of russian and I shouldn't have passed. The reason I did was because I sat outside the teachers office everyday after class with a TA and studied for an hour for the entire year. She knew I was working hard and so she let me pass. She later told me that she never had a student who was so bad but tried so hard.

Find a rhythm in the day that works for you and try to work classes and study time around that. For instance I found myself happiest when I went to bed at 3am and woke up at 10. Work and classes till 8 at night and then homework and chill till 3.

Have a dedicated time to hangout/blow of steam. While you need to stay on top of studying and all that you also need to relax. For instance I never did homework on Saturdays ever.

Rent books that aren't essential to your major or planned career path. Going into Microbiology? Probably won't need to keep that intro to history book but you may want to keep bio textbooks for reference later. Also look around town for other stores that sell text books, they'll be cheaper.

If your campus has a gym use it. You're already paying for it most likely and you'll put on weight because generally the food won't be healthy. Three things for food on campus are Healthy, cheap, tasty. Pick two.

You are going to do stupid shit. It'll happen so be ready for it. If this is your first time around alcohol/drugs try them in a safe place with people you trust in case you don't take to it.

College is billed as a place for you to ask questions and openly discuss but that may not be the case everywhere so just be aware.

It'll probably take a few weeks for you to get settled in so that's normal.
Organize, take notes so you can recreate the lecture, don't procrastinate, eat healthy, take multivitamins
